questions.q: Why can't block storage like Amazon EBS serve as shared training-data storage for a 64-node cluster?
options: It's too slow for any workload
An EBS volume attaches to a single compute instance, so it can't be read concurrently by many nodes
EBS doesn't support reading files, only writing
EBS volumes are limited to 1 GB in size
questions.explain: Block storage is a raw volume attached to one instance at a time — excellent for that node's local disk, but not something many nodes can mount and read together.

questions.q: What is the documented S3 request-rate baseline per partitioned prefix?
options: Unlimited requests per second with no partitioning needed
At least 3,500 PUT/COPY/POST/DELETE or 5,500 GET/HEAD requests per second, multiplying with more prefixes
A flat 100 requests per second regardless of prefix
S3 does not support concurrent requests
questions.explain: S3 supports at least 3,500 PUT/COPY/POST/DELETE or 5,500 GET/HEAD requests per second per partitioned prefix, and that scales further by spreading objects across more prefixes.

questions.q: What is a data repository association (DRA) in FSx for Lustre?
options: A Kubernetes RBAC role for storage access
A link between an FSx for Lustre filesystem and an S3 bucket that lazily loads objects on first read
A snapshot backup of an FSx filesystem
A billing relationship between AWS accounts
questions.explain: A DRA links an FSx for Lustre directory to an S3 bucket or prefix; the first read of a given object pulls it from S3 and caches it on FSx's own storage for low-latency reads after that.

questions.q: Why does the lesson describe Solara AI's storage strategy as 'both, in layers' rather than choosing S3 or FSx for Lustre alone?
options: Because FSx for Lustre cannot store any data permanently
Because S3 serves as the cheap, durable source of truth while FSx for Lustre acts as a high-throughput, low-latency cache in front of it
Because AWS requires using both services together by policy
Because block storage replaces the need for either
questions.explain: S3 holds every shard durably and cheaply; FSx for Lustre, linked via a DRA, caches the actively-read subset on fast storage — combining durability with low-latency reads.

questions.q: What throughput characteristic does FSx for Lustre offer that distinguishes it from S3's per-request model?
options: Unlimited free storage
Parallel I/O across many backing disks, reaching up to hundreds of GB/s in aggregate
Automatic model training without a GPU
Built-in version control for training scripts
questions.explain: As a parallel filesystem, FSx for Lustre spreads a single file's I/O across many disks concurrently, reaching aggregate throughput that a single consumer's per-request object-storage access pattern doesn't achieve.
